content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction guide, but it is presented in a fragmented and encoded format. Each interaction is described in detail, maintaining the original specificity and clinical relevance: 1. Unconjugated Estrogens (Vaginal): Vaginal estrogens may alter the metabolism of hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Darunavir and Copanlisib: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely. 3. Cobicistat and Copanlisib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Strong CYP3A Inhibitors and Copanlisib: If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg and monitor closely. 5. Darunavir and Cortisone: Darunavir increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while cortisone decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Crizotinib and Darunavir: Crizotinib increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases crizotinib levels similarly. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Cobicistat and Crizotinib: Cobicistat increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased crizotinib levels may lead to QT prolongation. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg daily and monitor closely. 8. Crofelermer and Darunavir: Crofelermer increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Crofelermer is minimally absorbed systemically, so systemic inhibition is unlikely. 9. Darunavir and Cyclophosphamide: Darunavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cyclophosphamide also increases darunavir levels. Monitor closely. 10. Cobicistat and Cyclophosphamide: Cobicistat increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 11. Cyclosporine and Darunavir: Cyclosporine increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and darunavir increases cyclosporine levels. Cobicistat also increases cyclosporine levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Darunavir and Dabigatran: Darunavir increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 13. Dabrafenib and Darunavir: Dabrafenib decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat and Dabrafenib: Cobicistat increases dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Danazol and Darunavir: Danazol increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Cobicistat and Dapsone: Cobicistat increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 17. Darunavir and Diazepam: Darunavir increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat and Diazepam: Cobicistat increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Darunavir and Didanosine: Darunavir decreases didanosine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer didanosine 1 hour before or 2 hours after darunavir/ritonavir. Monitor closely. 20. Darunavir and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Darunavir increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 21. Cobicistat and Digoxin: Cobicistat increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating concomitant drugs. Adjust the digoxin dose by 30-50% or modify dosing frequency. 22. Cobicistat and Dihydroergotamine: Cobicistat increases dihydroergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity. 23. Darunavir and Diltiazem: Darunavir increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for calcium channel blocker toxicities. 24. Cobicistat and Docetaxel: Cobicistat increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the docetaxel dose by 50% if coadministration cannot be avoided. 25. Darunavir and Dofetilide: Darunavir increases dofetilide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 26. Darunavir and Donepezil: Darunavir increases donepezil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 27. Cobicistat and Doravirine: Cobicistat increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for increased plasma concentrations and toxicities.
